messages.text: okay wait i was skimming your canvas loop code and thought... does it hurt to add a super subtle particle field in the background? like, tiny dots drifting? not stars, just dust. makes the turquoise glass feel less flat

hmm. depends on perf. if it's a static texture it's fine. if it's animated particles i need to know we're not going to tank the fps on the GX10 while ollama is chewing on embeddings. what density are we talking about?
like 5% of the screen area? barely visible. just enough to give depth. and yeah, if it lags we kill it instantly. i can make a toggle in dev mode too

5% is safe. i'll render them on a separate offscreen canvas so they don't dirty the main atlas layer. that way the sphere culling logic stays clean. also, the 'link' emblem for the viewer—do we have a final glyph for that yet? or am i still drawing a generic person icon?

generic person is dead to me. i want it to look like a link in a chain, but soft. like two interlocking curves instead of a hard circle. sends sketch in 5 mins. also the glass effect on the people bubbles needs to be more frosted right now, it looks too shiny

frosted is doable. i'll bump up the blur radius on the backdrop-filter. also, regarding the emblem: if it's two curves, is there a specific aspect ratio? i need to know if it fits in the 24px avatar circle without getting weird

square-ish. 1:1. here's the rough idea: imagine a lowercase 'i' made of two soft links. i'll send the svg in a sec. also john, you said 'dust' particles earlier? make sure they don't overlap the text labels, it'll be unreadable

copy that. i'll add a z-index hierarchy so text is always on top and particles are behind everything except the background color. sending you the svg when it lands in my inbox. btw, the frosted glass is looking way better. feels premium now

yes!! that's it. the 'premium' feeling is what we're going for. i'm going to tweak the opacity of the particles to 0.15 so they are almost subliminal. this looks like a product, not a student project anymore. seriously though, i'm proud

same. the 'why you connect' tooltip popping over that frosted glass is going to hit hard in the demo. i just pushed the particle toggle to the settings object so we can flip it off if the judges' laptops are slow. should be safe now
smart. okay, i'm done for the night. going to stare at this turquoise void and feel calm. don't break the layout before tomorrow! good luck with the force-directed spacing
will do. i'm actually going to let it settle for an hour in the background and screenshot the stable state. night mei
